oneLiner: The only foundry that can make and package leading-edge AI silicon at volume, growing ~44% this year at a ~51% net margin. The market prices it as if that growth fades fast: it is betting that 2027 is a digestion year and that today's margins are a cyclical peak.

verdict.summary: TSMC's Q3 2026 beat guidance, the Q4 guide steps revenue up another ~14% sequentially, and full-year growth is now ~44% in USD. Management still says AI demand is far above what it can supply. The stock is valued as though growth slows sharply: the reverse DCF needs ~6% a year against ~19% delivered over the last three years. That leaves room for a base case of ~30% FY2027 growth at a low-20s multiple to return low double digits. The bear case needs both a 2027 digestion and margin compression from N2, overseas fabs and tool inflation. Two things would change the view: a January 2027 guide pointing to growth under 15%, or a gross margin guide below 64%.
wtb: FY2027 revenue grows at least 25% in USD (to ~$220B+ on FY2026's ~$176B) as 2nm capacity more than doubles and CoWoS roughly doubles.
Gross margin holds at or above 65% through the 2nm ramp and Arizona fab 2 start-up (overseas dilution ~2% now, 3-4% later).
2027 capex lands near the $85-90B brokerage range rather than well above it, so FCF keeps growing alongside revenue.
At end-2027 the market pays at least ~20x FY2027 EPS per ADR, which needs only 2028 growth to look positive.

bear.why: Hyperscalers digest 2026's build in 2027 and consumer and price-sensitive segments weaken on component inflation, the risk management itself flagged. Revenue grows only ~11%. N2 ramp costs, overseas fabs, tool inflation and a stronger NT dollar take net margin to ~47%. With record capex landing into slowing demand, the market goes back to a cyclical, Taiwan-discounted multiple.

base.why: 2nm capacity more than doubles and blended wafer prices rise as brokerages expect. Revenue grows ~31%, close to the 2026 run-rate fading. Net margin holds ~51% as pricing offsets dilution. Growth in 2028 still looks positive, so the market pays a low-20s multiple, near the stock's recent range and well above its decade norm.

bull.why: The AI accelerator and custom-ASIC ramp (Rubin, MI400, Broadcom and Google XPUs) keeps wafers and CoWoS sold out through 2027. Revenue grows ~45%, matching 2026. Price increases carry net margin to ~53%. Packaging scarcity and the lack of a viable second source earn a mid-20s multiple.

scenarioModel.note: FY2026 revenue = Q1 $35.9B + Q2 $40.2B + Q3 $46.7B + Q4 guide midpoint $53.3B = ~$176B (~44% USD growth). EPS is per ADR in USD: 1 ADR = 5 common shares, so ~25.93B diluted common shares = ~5.19B ADR units. EPS = revenue x net margin / 5.19B. Bear 195 x 47% / 5.19 = $17.66; base 230 x 51% / 5.19 = $22.60; bull 255 x 53% / 5.19 = $26.04. Q3 2026 was US$4.60 per ADR at a 51.1% net margin. Multiples are applied to FY2027 EPS at end-2027. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Is 2027 a growth year or a digestion year?
debates.bull: AI demand is 'far above' supply per C.C. Wei, 2nm capacity more than doubles in 2027, Goldman sees CoWoS capacity rising ~114% in 2027, and customer roadmaps (Rubin, Broadcom XPUs) are fixed a year ahead.
debates.bear: Management is 'being prudent in its planning for 2027', citing component-price pressure on consumer and price-sensitive segments and macro uncertainty. HPC is 68% of revenue, so a hyperscaler pause hits harder than in any prior cycle.
debates.view: This debate sets both revenue and the multiple. The prudence comment is about smartphone and PC units, not AI, and AI is where capacity is sold out. We weight growth of 25%+ at 55%.

signpost.metric: TSMC FY2027 USD revenue growth guide; combined 2027 hyperscaler capex guidance
signpost.threshold: bullish if TSMC guides 25%+; bearish if it guides under 15% or hyperscaler 2027 capex is flat
signpost.when: Hyperscaler Q3 calls Oct 28-30, 2026; TSMC Q4 report, mid-Jan 2027

debates.q: Can gross margin hold above 65% through the 2nm ramp?
debates.bull: Q3's 66.4% was inside the 65-67% guide even with initial 2nm dilution. Brokerages see 2027 gross margin of 66.7-68.9% as blended wafer prices rise, and UBS argues TSMC can pass tool inflation through to customers.
debates.bear: Gross margin has fallen from Q2's 67.7%. 2nm at 8% of wafer revenue is dilutive while it ramps, overseas dilution widens to 3-4%, and 'tool inflation is real'. Each point of margin is ~$2.3B of FY2027 operating profit.
debates.view: We expect a low-to-mid 60s floor, not a cliff, because pricing power is the moat. The bear case needs margin below 64% and slowing growth together.

signpost.metric: Q4 2026 gross margin and Q1 2027 gross margin guide
signpost.threshold: bearish if the Q1 2027 guide midpoint is below 64%; bullish if 66%+

debates.q: Does the capex step-up earn its return or signal overbuild?
debates.bull: Capex follows customer commitments. TTM capex/revenue is ~34%, below the 48% of 2022, and FCF covers it with ~$78B of net cash left over.
debates.bear: Brokerages see 2027 capex of $83-90B (+40-45%) and up to $105B in 2028, as TSMC guides 2026-2028 spend 'significantly higher' than 2023-2025. Foundry overbuilds have ended every prior upcycle.
debates.view: Capex intensity is not the risk while it stays under ~40% of revenue. Spending that rises faster than revenue guidance would be.

signpost.metric: FY2027 capex guide vs FY2027 revenue growth guide
signpost.threshold: bearish if capex growth exceeds revenue growth by 20+ points (capex/revenue above ~40%)

thesis: Nobody else ships leading-edge at volume. 2nm went from 3% to 8% of wafer revenue in one quarter and capacity more than doubles in 2027, while Intel 18A and Samsung SF2 are still fixing yields. 79% of wafer revenue is now at 7nm and below.
Pricing power offsets dilution. Gross margin has stayed in a 66-68% band through a new node ramp and overseas start-ups, and brokerages expect blended wafer prices to rise again in 2027.

The price assumes a slowdown the business has not shown. The reverse DCF needs ~6% a year earnings growth against ~19% a year revenue growth over the last three years, and operating margin expanded ~10 points over four quarters.

Packaging is a second gate TSMC controls. CoWoS remains customers' first choice (C.C. Wei), and capacity is expected to roughly double in 2027 (Goldman Sachs), so packaging limits rivals as much as wafers do.

latestQuarter.label: Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep; reported Oct 15, 2026)
points: Revenue US$46.72B, +41.2% YoY, +16.2% QoQ (NT$1,494.24B, +50.9% YoY), above the $44.6-45.8B guide.
Gross margin 66.4% (guide 65-67%), operating margin 58.7%, net margin 51.1%; net income NT$763.06B (+68.7% YoY).
Diluted EPS NT$29.43, US$4.60 per ADR (+68.7% YoY).
Node mix: 2nm 8%, 3nm 33%, 5nm 28%, 7nm 10%. Platform: HPC 68% (+22% QoQ), smartphone 21% (+10%), automotive 4% (+23%).
Q3 capex US$13.8B; 2026 capex held at US$60-64B.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (reported Oct 15). Revenue US$46.72B, +41.2% YoY and +16.2% QoQ, beat the guide's top end by ~$0.9B. Gross margin of 66.4% was 130bp lower q/q, the first quarter of 2026 inside the 65-67% guide rather than above it, as the 2nm ramp began to dilute. Operating margin was 58.7%. EPS was NT$29.43 (US$4.60 per ADR). HPC rose 22% q/q to 68% of revenue, and 2nm went from 3% to 8% of wafer revenue in one quarter. Net income grew only 8% q/q against 17.6% revenue growth (NT$), so the step down in net margin is worth watching next quarter. C.C. Wei repeated that AI demand remains far above what TSMC can supply. He also said the company is being prudent in its 2027 planning because component-price inflation is pressuring consumer and price-sensitive segments.
guidanceProse: Q4 2026 guide: revenue US$52.3-54.3B, gross margin 65-67%, operating margin 56.5-58.5%, at US$1 = NT$31.8. That implies ~44% USD growth for FY2026, raised from 'slightly above 40%'. 2026 capex stays at US$60-64B (raised in July from $52-56B). Management said 2026-2028 capex will be significantly higher than 2023-2025 and that tool inflation is real. Brokerage 2027 estimates run $83-90B (Morgan Stanley $83B, Goldman and BofA ~$85B, UBS ~$90B); TSMC has given no 2027 number. Overseas-fab gross margin dilution is now ~2%, widening to 3-4% later in the five-year period. Arizona fab 2 begins volume production in Q3 2027, slightly ahead of plan.
segments: HPC 68% of Q3 2026 revenue (+22% QoQ): AI accelerators, custom ASICs, server CPUs.
Smartphone 21% (+10% QoQ): fall 2026 flagship silicon on N3/N2. This is the segment exposed to component-price pressure in 2027.
Automotive 4% (+23% QoQ); IoT and other make up the remainder.
competitive: Intel 18A is in volume but targets world-class yields only by 2027. Intel's EMIB packaging is the 'very competitive' alternative to CoWoS that Wei acknowledged.
Samsung SF2 is prioritizing GAA yield recovery over leapfrogging.
Reported N2 pricing near $30K per wafer with capacity booked into 2028 (trade press, unverified).
Practically every leading AI accelerator (NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, Broadcom XPUs, Trainium, Cerebras) is fabbed here, and customers name wafers, substrates and HBM as their binding constraints.
moat: Process leadership, yield and scale economics, advanced-packaging control, and an ecosystem of PDKs, IP and design services that makes switching foundries a multi-year project. 2nm sold out before it ramped, and a 66%+ gross margin through a node transition shows pricing power no rival foundry has.
risks: Taiwan concentration. Leading-edge capacity is still overwhelmingly in Taiwan. Arizona (fab 2 volume Q3 2027) and the US-Taiwan trade deal (15% tariff, $250B of planned Taiwanese US investment) reduce the discount but do not remove it.

AI capex cyclicality. With HPC at 68% of revenue, a hyperscaler digestion year would hit harder than any prior foundry downturn. Management's 'prudent' 2027 stance is the first hedge in its language this cycle.
Capex escalation. 2026 capex of $60-64B is already above the original $52-56B plan, and 2027 estimates of $83-90B would put capex near 40% of revenue if growth slows.

Margin dilution stacking. 2nm ramp costs, overseas dilution widening to 3-4%, tool inflation and NT dollar strength (USD revenue, NTD costs) all push the same way. Gross margin is already off its Q2 high.
Customer concentration. Apple, NVIDIA and Broadcom are each large, single-name dependencies, and a design-win shift on any one would show up within a year.
catalysts: Oct 28-30, 2026: MSFT, GOOGL, META, AMZN Q3 calls - 2027 capex framing (debate 1).
~Nov 10 and ~Dec 10, 2026: October and November monthly revenue, tracking the Q4 guide (debate 1).
~Nov 18, 2026: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 report - Rubin ramp on N3 and CoWoS (debate 1).
Mid-Jan 2027: TSMC Q4 2026 report - FY2027 growth, gross margin and capex guidance (debates 1, 2, 3).
Q3 2027: Arizona fab 2 volume production; 2nm capacity doubling through 2027 (debate 2).

valPresets.note: Valuation basis is forward earnings, not FCF: TTM FCF is structurally depressed by a $60-64B 2026 capex program heading higher in 2027, which would make an FCF-DCF read absurdly demanding.

notes: Statement history shown is 4 years (Yahoo) because TSMC files 20-F/6-K rather than 10-K/10-Q; figures converted from TWD at spot. FCF here is capex-heavy: the valuation lab base case uses normalized growth off a depressed FCF base.
